item.title: Ostrik's Theorem for Operator Algebras in a Unitary Tensor Category
item.description: arXiv:2611.13424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define Hilbert modules for $\mathrm{C^*}$ and $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebra objects in the ind-completion of a unitary tensor category. We then prove an operator algebraic Ostrik's theorem in an ind-category: the 2-category of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebras objects, their modules, and adjointable intertwiners is $\dagger$-equivalent to the 2-categories of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ module categories.
item.dc:creator: Emeline Sherman

item.title: $\mathbb{R}$-linear unitary preservers of C$^*$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.13822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the structure of general $\mathbb{R}$-linear unitary preservers between unital C$^*$-algebras. Representing any unital $\mathbb{R}$-linear unitary preserver in terms of three $\mathbb{R}$-linear maps on the self-adjoint part of the domain yields a canonical decomposition into a Jordan-type summand and a purely non-Jordan summand. When the domain is abelian, we completely classify the purely non-Jordan summand via type $\mathrm{I}_2$ JW-algebras. For unital C$^*$-algebras with no two-dimensional irreducible representations, we characterize a natural class of purely non-Jordan unitary preservers governed by pairs of Jordan $*$-homomorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Lu Cui, Wenming Wu, Wei Yuan

item.title: An Equivariant Coarse Green-Julg Theorem for Proper Actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an equivariant coarse Green--Julg theorem for proper isometric actions of countable discrete groups on bounded geometry metric spaces. We introduce the $(\Gamma, X)$-controlled proper $C^{*}$-algebra, and show that the evaluation-at-zero map between the equivariant localization and Roe algebras with such coefficients induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Qin Wang, Chen Zhang

item.title: Morita equivalence classes for crossed product of rational rotation algebras
item.description: arXiv:2505.19869v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Morita equivalence classes of crossed products of rotation algebras $A_\theta$, where $\theta$ is a rational number, by finite and infinite cyclic subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$. We show that for any such subgroup $F$, the crossed products $A_\theta \rtimes F$ and $A_{\theta'} \rtimes F$ are strongly Morita equivalent, where both $\theta$ and $\theta'$ are rational. Combined with previous results for irrational values of $\theta$, our result provides a complete classification of the crossed products $A_\theta \rtimes F$ up to Morita equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Chakraborty, Pratik Kumar Kundu

item.title: Cocycle perturbations and ergodicity for actions on type III factors
item.description: arXiv:2512.12931v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study cocycle perturbations of state preserving actions on type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factors. Extending the theorem of Marrakchi and Vaes for type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors, we show that a state preserving outer $\mathbb Z$-action on a type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor with trivial bicentralizer admits a unitary cocycle whose perturbation becomes an ergodic action. This partially answers a question of Marrakchi and Vaes. A major difference from the type $\mathrm{II}$ case is that the modular automorphism group naturally appears as part of the action, making the construction of the required cocycle more delicate.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Isono

item.title: Partial factorization and reflexivity of operator algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.27479v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable infinite dimensional Hilbert space and $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ the algebra of all bounded linear operators on $\mathcal{H}$. A subalgebra $\mathfrak{A}$ in $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ has the left (resp.\ right) partial factorization property if for any invertible operator $S\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$, there exists an isometry (resp.\ a co-isometry) $U\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ such that $U^*S, S^{-1}U\in\mathfrak{A}$. We show that if $\mathfrak{A}$ is weak operator topology closed with the left (resp.\ right) partial factorization property, then $\mathfrak{A}$ is the nest algebra associated with its invariant subspace lattice. In particular, if $\mathfrak{A}$ is transitive, then $\mathfrak{A}=\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$. This gives a positive answer to Question 6.3 raised by B.V.R. Bhat and M. Kumar in \emph{Publ. Res. Inst. Math. Sci.} \textbf{60}(2024), 507--537.
item.dc:creator: Fengyang Jia, Guoxing Ji

item.title: The generator problem for C*-algebras with comparison
item.description: arXiv:2610.13792v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that certain classes of unital, simple, separable C*-algebras with comparison are singly generated, including tracially AF algebras and monotracial crossed products of actions on the Cantor space. In particular, we show that simple, separable, tracially AF algebras have generator rank one.
item.dc:creator: Ben Bouwen, Jorge Castillejos, Jakub Curda

item.title: Characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the annulus
item.description: arXiv:2610.40118v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish algebraic characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space on the annulus. As an application, we characterize compact perturbations of Toeplitz operators and prove a zero-product result.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Adhikari, Susmita Das, Shubham Jain, Jaydeb Sarkar

item.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
item.description: arXiv:2611.01503v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain the complete bound $2$, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.
item.dc:creator: Mihai Putinar, Georgios Tsikalas
